title.zh: 卷32 列傳第24 申徽 陸通 弟逞 柳敏 盧柔 唐瑾
title.en: Volume 32 Biographies 24: Shen Hui; Lu Tong; younger brother Cheng; Liu Min; Lu Rou; Tang Jin
title.raw: 卷32 列傳第24 申徽 陸通 弟逞 柳敏 盧柔 唐瑾 Volume 32 Biographies 24: Shen Hui; Lu Tong; younger brother Cheng; Liu Min; Lu Rou; Tang Jin

sentences.zh: 申徽 陸通 弟逞 柳敏 盧柔 唐瑾

translations.literal: Shen Hui; Lu Tong; younger brother Cheng; Liu Min; Lu Rou; Tang Jin
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Shen Hui, Lu Tong, Lu Cheng, Liu Min, Lu Rou, and Tang Jin

sentences.zh: 申徽字世儀，魏郡人也。

translations.literal: Shen Hui, styled Shiyi, was a native of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Hui, courtesy name Shiyi, came from Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖鐘，為後趙司徒。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Zhong served as Grand Minister of the Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, Zhong had served the Later Zhao as grand minister.

sentences.zh: 冉閔末，中原喪亂，鐘子邃避地江左。

translations.literal: At the end of Ran Min's reign, when the Central Plains were in chaos, Zhong's son Sui fled south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When Ran Min fell and the heartland collapsed into chaos, Zhong's son Sui fled south across the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 曾祖爽仕宋，位雍州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shuang served Song and held the post of Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shuang had served the Liu-Song court as inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 祖隆道，宋北兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Longdao was Northern Yanzhou Inspector under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Longdao had been northern inspector of Yan Province under Song.

sentences.zh: 父明仁，郡功曹，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Mingren was a commandery merit officer; he died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mingren served as a commandery merit officer and died young.

sentences.zh: 徽少與母居，盡心孝養。

translations.literal: In youth Hui lived with his mother and devoted himself to filial care.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he lived alone with his mother and cared for her with complete devotion.

sentences.zh: 及長，好經史。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he loved the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he took to the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 性審慎，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: His nature was cautious; he did not associate casually.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful by temperament and would not keep company lightly.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，喪畢，乃歸於魏。

translations.literal: After his mother's death, when mourning was complete, he returned to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning for his mother was finished, he went back to Wei territory.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以元邃為東徐州刺史，邃引徽為主簿。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yuan Sui was made Eastern Xu Province Inspector; Sui brought Hui in as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang, Yuan Sui was made inspector of Eastern Xu Province and took Hui on as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，邃被檻車送洛陽，故吏賓客並委去，唯徽送之。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated, Sui was sent to Luoyang in a caged cart; former subordinates and guests all abandoned him—only Hui escorted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Hao's defeat Sui was carted off to Luoyang in a prisoner's cage; former staff and guests all deserted him, and only Hui went along.

sentences.zh: 及邃得免，乃廣集賓友，歎徽有古人風。

translations.literal: When Sui was released, he gathered guests and friends widely and praised Hui's ancient-style integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sui was cleared, he called a great gathering of friends and guests and praised Hui for the bearing of men of old.

sentences.zh: 尋除太尉府行參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed acting adjutant in the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting adjutant in the grand marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，徽以洛陽兵難未已，遂間行入關見文帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, because military turmoil in Luoyang had not ended, Hui traveled by secret routes into the Pass to see Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, with Luoyang still torn by war, Hui stole by hidden paths into the Pass to see Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 文帝與語，奇之，薦之於賀拔岳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen spoke with him, marveled at him, and recommended him to Heba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai talked with him, was struck by his quality, and recommended him to Heba Yue.

sentences.zh: 岳亦雅相敬待，引為賓客。

translations.literal: Yue too treated him with refined respect and took him in as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Heba Yue likewise received him with marked respect and kept him as a guest.

sentences.zh: 文帝臨夏州，以徽為記室參軍，兼府主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took up post at Xia Province, he made Hui recording secretary adjutant and concurrently chief clerk of the commandery office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai assumed charge at Xia Province, he made Hui recording secretary and also chief clerk of the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 文帝察徽沉密有度量，每事信委之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen saw that Hui was deep, discreet, and measured; in every matter he trusted and delegated to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai found him grave, close-mouthed, and steady in judgment, and in every affair relied on him fully.

sentences.zh: 乃為大行臺郎中。

translations.literal: He was then made gentleman of the Grand Military Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: He was next appointed gentleman of the grand military commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 時軍國草創，幕府務殷，四方書檄，皆徽之辭也。

translations.literal: At that time the army and state were newly founded; the headquarters was busy; documents and proclamations from all quarters were all in Hui's phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: The realm and its armies were still being built from nothing; the staff was overwhelmed with work, and dispatches from every direction went out in Hui's words.

sentences.zh: 以迎孝武功，封博平縣子，本州大中正。

translations.literal: For merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Booping and made grand rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: For service in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu he was enfeoffed viscount of Booping county and made grand rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 大統初，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, his rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Datong era his title was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜中書舍人，修起居注。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed palace secretary and compiled the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became palace secretary and took charge of the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 河橋之役，大軍不利，近侍之官，分散者衆，徽獨不離左右。

translations.literal: At the Battle of He Bridge the main army fared badly; many attendants scattered—Hui alone did not leave the side.
translations.idiomatic: At He Bridge the main force met disaster; attendants at court fled in numbers, but Hui alone never left his lord's side.

sentences.zh: 魏帝稱歎之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor commended him for it.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to attendant at the Gates as supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was moved to supervising secretary and attendant at the gates.

sentences.zh: 先是，東陽王元榮為瓜州刺史，其女婿劉彥隨焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Dongyang Yuan Rong had been Inspector of Gua Province; his son-in-law Liu Yan accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Some time before, Prince Dongyang Yuan Rong had been inspector of Gua Province, and his son-in-law Liu Yan had gone with him.

sentences.zh: 及榮死，瓜州首望表榮子康為刺史，彥遂殺康而取其位。

translations.literal: When Rong died, the leading families of Gua Province petitioned for Rong's son Kang as inspector; Yan then killed Kang and seized the post.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong's death the leading men of Gua Province petitioned to make Rong's son Kang inspector, but Yan murdered Kang and took the office for himself.

sentences.zh: 屬四方多難，朝廷不遑問罪，因授彥刺史。

translations.literal: Because troubles were many in all quarters, the court had no leisure to punish him and therefore invested Yan as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: With rebellion everywhere, the court could not spare troops to punish him and so confirmed Yan as inspector.

sentences.zh: 頻征不奉詔，又南通吐谷渾，將圖叛逆。

translations.literal: Repeatedly summoned, he did not obey the edict; he also allied south with Tuyuhun and intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Called to court again and again, he refused the summons; he also opened ties south to Tuyuhun and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 文帝難於動衆，欲以權略致之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen found it difficult to move troops and wished to bring him in by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai hesitated to commit a large force and hoped to take him by craft instead.

sentences.zh: 乃以徽為河西大使，密令圖彥。

translations.literal: He therefore made Hui envoy to Hexi and secretly ordered him to take Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore sent Hui as envoy to Hexi with secret orders to seize Yan.

sentences.zh: 徽輕以五十騎行，旣至，止於賓館。

translations.literal: Hui traveled lightly with fifty riders; when he arrived, he lodged at the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rode in lightly with only fifty horsemen, and on arrival put up at the official guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 彥見徽單使，不以為疑。

translations.literal: Yan saw Hui had come alone as envoy and did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan saw that Hui had come as a lone envoy and raised no suspicion.

sentences.zh: 徽乃遣一人微勸彥歸朝，以揣其意。

translations.literal: Hui then sent one man to gently urge Yan to return to court, to probe his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then sent a man to coax Yan toward returning to court, testing his mind.

sentences.zh: 彥不從。

translations.literal: Yan would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 徽又使贊成其住計，彥便從之，遂來至館。

translations.literal: Hui again had someone endorse his plan to stay put; Yan then agreed and came to the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Hui next had someone praise his plan to remain where he was; Yan accepted and came to the lodge.

sentences.zh: 徽先與瓜州豪右密謀執彥，遂叱而縛之。

translations.literal: Hui had first conspired in secret with the magnates of Gua Province to seize Yan; he then shouted and bound him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had already plotted with Gua Province's local powers to arrest Yan; now he cried out and had him bound.

sentences.zh: 彥辭無罪。

translations.literal: Yan pleaded innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Yan protested that he was guiltless.

sentences.zh: 徽數之曰：「君無尺寸之功，濫居方嶽之重。

translations.literal: Hui rebuked him, saying, "You have not an inch of merit yet hold a regional commander's weight unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rebuked him: "You have done nothing to earn even a finger's breadth of credit, yet you usurp a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 恃遠背誕，不恭貢職，戮辱使人，輕忽詔命。

translations.literal: You rely on distance to rebel, fail in tribute duties, humiliate envoys, and treat edicts lightly.
translations.idiomatic: You trust in remoteness to defy the throne, neglect tribute, abuse imperial messengers, and treat edicts with contempt.

sentences.zh: 計君之咎，實不容誅。

translations.literal: Weighing your offenses, they truly should not spare execution.
translations.idiomatic: Tally your crimes, and death would barely suffice.

sentences.zh: 但授詔之日，本令相送歸闕，所恨不得申明罰以謝邊遠耳。

translations.literal: But on the day the edict was issued, it was originally ordered that I escort you back to court; my only regret is that I could not make clear the punishment to appease the distant border."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the day I received my orders I was told only to escort you back to the capital; my one regret is that I cannot pronounce sentence here and satisfy the far frontier."

sentences.zh: 」於是宣詔慰勞吏人及彥所部，復云大軍續至，城內無敢動者。

translations.literal: Thereupon he proclaimed the edict, reassuring officials and people and Yan's troops, and added that a great army would follow; none in the city dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: He then read out the edict, reassuring officials, commoners, and Yan's men, and declared that a great army was close behind; no one in the city dared move.

sentences.zh: 使還，遷都官尚書。

translations.literal: Returning from the mission, he was transferred to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When he came back from the mission he was made minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 十二年，瓜州刺史成慶為城人張保所殺，都督令狐延等起義逐保，啟請刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Gua Province Inspector Cheng Qing was killed by Zhang Bao, a man of the city; Area Commander Linghu Yan and others raised forces, drove out Bao, and petitioned for an inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the inspector of Gua Province, Cheng Qing, was murdered by a townsman named Zhang Bao; area commander Linghu Yan and others rose up, expelled Bao, and asked the court for a new inspector.

sentences.zh: 以徽信洽西土，拜假節、瓜州刺史。

translations.literal: Because Hui was trusted and well regarded in the western lands, he was invested with provisional credentials and made Inspector of Gua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hui was trusted throughout the west, he received provisional credentials and was appointed inspector of Gua Province.

sentences.zh: 徽在州五稔，儉約率下，邊人樂而安之。

translations.literal: Hui was in the province five harvest-years; frugal and leading by example, the border people took joy in him and were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hui governed the province for five years, living plainly and setting the tone himself; the frontier people were glad under him and lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 十六年，征兼尚書右僕射，加侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was summoned and made acting Right Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, with added titles attendant-in-ordinary, general of fast cavalry, and opener of the way with equal third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was recalled and made acting right vice minister of the masters of writing, with the added ranks of attendant-in-ordinary, general of fast cavalry, and opener of the way with equal third rank.

sentences.zh: 廢帝二年，進爵為公，正右僕射，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: In the second year of the deposed emperor, his rank was advanced to duke; he became regular right vice minister and was granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the deposed emperor his title rose to duke; he became full right vice minister and was granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 徽性勤敏，凡所居官，案牘無大小，皆親自省覽。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was diligent and quick; in every office he held, documents large and small, he personally examined them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was industrious and alert; in every post he held he read every document himself, no matter how small.

sentences.zh: 以是事無稽滯，吏不得為姦。

translations.literal: Because of this business met no delay; clerks could not work deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing piled up unattended, and clerks had no room for fraud.

sentences.zh: 後雖歷公卿，此志不懈。

translations.literal: Though afterward he passed through ducal and ministerial ranks, this resolve never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose through the highest offices, he never let that habit slip.

sentences.zh: 出為襄州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 時南方初附，舊俗，官人皆通餉遺。

translations.literal: At that time the south had newly submitted; by old custom officials all exchanged gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The south had only lately submitted, and by long custom local officials all passed gifts back and forth.

sentences.zh: 徽性廉慎，乃畫楊震像於寢室以自戒。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was incorrupt and careful; he painted a portrait of Yang Zhen in his bedchamber to warn himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was scrupulous and wary of corruption; he hung a portrait of Yang Zhen in his sleeping room to keep himself honest.

sentences.zh: 及代還，人吏送者數十裏不絕。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned, officials and people escorted him for several tens of li without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour ended and he set out for the capital, officials and commoners followed him for dozens of li without breaking off.

sentences.zh: 徽自以無德於人，慨然懷愧，因賦詩題於清水亭。

translations.literal: Hui felt he had done no virtue for the people, sighed with shame, and composed a poem inscribed at Qingshui Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Hui felt he had given the people too little, flushed with shame, and wrote a poem he left inscribed at Qingshui Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 長幼聞之，競來就讀。

translations.literal: Young and old hearing it competed to come and read it.
translations.idiomatic: Old and young alike heard of it and rushed to read it.

sentences.zh: 遞相謂曰：「此是申使君手跡。

translations.literal: They told one another, "This is Prefect Shen's own hand.
translations.idiomatic: They said to one another, "These are Prefect Shen's own lines.

sentences.zh: 」並寫誦之。

translations.literal: " They all copied and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone copied them out and committed them to memory.

sentences.zh: 明帝以御正任總絲綸，更崇其秩為上大夫，員四人，號大御正，又以徽為之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, because the office of Director Rectifier oversaw edicts and measures, elevated its rank to senior grand master, four incumbents, titled Grand Director Rectifier; Hui was again appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, finding that the director rectifier controlled imperial edicts and policy, raised the office to senior grand master with four holders, called grand director rectifier, and again appointed Hui to it.

sentences.zh: 曆小司空、少保，出為荊州刺史，入為小司徒、小宗伯。

translations.literal: He passed through Junior Minister of Works and Junior Guardian; went out as Inspector of Jing Province; came in as Junior Minister of Worship and Junior Minister of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He served as junior minister of works and junior guardian, went out as inspector of Jing Province, and returned as junior minister of worship and junior minister of ritual.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，上疏乞骸骨，詔許之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he memorialized begging to retire; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he submitted a memorial asking to retire on account of age; the throne granted it.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈泗州刺史，諡曰章。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Inspector of Si Province; posthumous name Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made inspector of Si Province, with the posthumous name Zhang.

sentences.zh: 子康嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kang inherited his place.

sentences.zh: 位瀘州刺史，司織下大夫、上開府。

translations.literal: He held the post of Inspector of Lu Province, lower grand master of palace weaving, and upper opener of the way.
translations.idiomatic: He served as inspector of Lu Province, lower grand master of palace weaving, and upper opener of the way.

sentences.zh: 康弟敦，汝南郡守。

translations.literal: Kang's younger brother Dun was Administrator of Runan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's younger brother Dun was administrator of Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 敦弟靜，齊安郡守。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Jing was Administrator of Qi'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Jing was administrator of Qi'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 靜弟處，上開府、同昌縣侯。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Chu was upper opener of the way and Marquis of Tongchang county.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's younger brother Chu was upper opener of the way and marquis of Tongchang county.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 陸通字仲明，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Lu Tong, styled Zhongming, was a native of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong, courtesy name Zhongming, came from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖載，從宋武帝平關中，軍還，留載隨其子義真鎮長安，遂沒赫連氏。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zai followed Emperor Wu of Song in pacifying Guanzhong; when the army returned, Zai was left to follow his son Yizhen in garrisoning Chang'an and was thus lost to Helian's clan.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zai had marched with Emperor Wu of Song to pacify Guanzhong; when the army withdrew, Zai was left behind with Yizhen to hold Chang'an and was swallowed up by the Helian regime.

sentences.zh: 魏太武平赫連氏，載仕魏任中山郡守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiwu of Wei pacified Helian's clan, Zai served Wei and was made Administrator of Zhongshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taiwu of Wei destroyed the Helian, Zai entered Wei service and became administrator of Zhongshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父政，性至孝。

translations.literal: His father Zheng's nature was supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng was profoundly filial by nature.

sentences.zh: 其母吳人，好食魚，北土魚少，政求之常苦難。

translations.literal: His mother was a Wu native and loved to eat fish; in the northern lands fish were scarce, and Zheng's efforts to obtain them were often painfully difficult.
translations.idiomatic: His mother came from Wu and loved fish; in the north fish were hard to come by, and Zheng's search for them was often a bitter struggle.

sentences.zh: 後宅側忽有泉出而有魚，遂得以供膳。

translations.literal: Later beside the house a spring suddenly appeared with fish in it, and he was thus able to supply her meals.
translations.idiomatic: Then a spring broke out beside the house with fish in it, and at last he could set fish before her every day.

sentences.zh: 時人以為孝感所致，因謂其泉為孝魚泉。

translations.literal: People of the time took it as filial feeling moving heaven; they therefore called the spring the Filial Fish Spring.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day called it heaven's answer to filial devotion and named the spring the Filial Fish Spring.

sentences.zh: 初從爾朱天光討伐，及天光敗，歸文帝。

translations.literal: At first he followed Erzhu Tianguang on campaigns; when Tianguang was defeated, he came to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zheng campaigned under Erzhu Tianguang; when Tianguang fell, he entered Yuwen Tai's service.

sentences.zh: 文帝為行臺，以政為行臺左丞、原州長史，賜爵中都縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen became military commissioner, he made Zheng left assistant of the commissionerate and chief administrator of Yuan Province, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Zhongdu county.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Tai took command as military commissioner, he made Zheng left assistant of the commissionerate and chief administrator of Yuan Province and enfeoffed him baron of Zhongdu county.

sentences.zh: 大統中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Datong era, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Datong era.

sentences.zh: 又從解洛陽圍。

translations.literal: Again, he followed [them to] break the siege of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tong also marched when the siege of Luoyang was lifted.

sentences.zh: 軍還，屬趙青雀反于長安，文帝將討之，以人馬疲弊，不可速行。

translations.literal: The army returned; at that time Zhao Qingque rebelled at Chang'an; Emperor Wen was about to suppress him, but because men and horses were worn out, they could not march quickly.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home Zhao Qingque rose in rebellion at Chang'an; Yuwen Tai meant to crush him, but men and horses were exhausted and could not be hurried.

sentences.zh: 又謂青雀等一時陸梁，不足為慮。

translations.literal: He also considered Qingque and the like momentary insolent rebels, not worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: He also judged Qingque and his sort to be momentary upstarts and no serious threat.

sentences.zh: 乃雲：「我到長安，但輕騎臨之，必當面縛。

translations.literal: He therefore declared: "When I reach Chang'an, with light cavalry alone I will confront them—they will surely be bound before me.
translations.idiomatic: So he said openly, "When I reach Chang'an I need only ride up with a light detachment—they will be trussed up before my face.

sentences.zh: 」通進曰：「青雀等旣以大軍不利，謂朝廷傾危，同惡相求，遂成反亂。

translations.literal: " Tong stepped forward and said: "Since Qingque and the rest saw the main army's setback, they believe the court is tottering; like evils seeking one another, they have formed rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " Tong stepped forward: "Qingque and his fellows saw our main force defeated and think the dynasty is failing; birds of a feather, they have turned to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 然其逆謀久定，必無遷善之心。

translations.literal: Yet their rebel plot is long settled; surely they have no mind to turn toward good.
translations.idiomatic: Their treason has been long in the making; they will not turn back to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 且其詐言大軍敗績，東寇將至，若以輕騎往，百姓謂為信然，更沮兆庶之望。

translations.literal: Moreover they falsely claim the great army was destroyed and eastern enemies will arrive; if you go with light cavalry, the people will take it as true and lose hope all the more.
translations.idiomatic: They are already spreading lies that the great army was wiped out and eastern invaders are coming; if you ride in lightly, the people will believe it and lose heart completely.

sentences.zh: 大兵雖疲弊，精銳猶多。

translations.literal: The main army is worn, but elite troops remain many.
translations.idiomatic: Our force is tired, but we still have plenty of crack troops.

sentences.zh: 以明公之威，率思歸之衆，以順討逆，何慮不平。

translations.literal: With your lordship's authority, leading people who long to return, punishing rebels in the name of order—what worry that it will not be pacified?"
translations.idiomatic: With your authority, leading men who yearn to come home, taking the righteous path against rebels—what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 」文帝深納之，因從平青雀。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen deeply accepted this and therefore followed to pacify Qingque.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai took the counsel to heart and marched with him to put down Qingque.

sentences.zh: 錄前後功，進爵為公，徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Recording his services before and after, his rank was advanced to duke and he was made Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier and later achievements were entered on the rolls; he was raised to duke and made inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 以寇難未平，留不之部。

translations.literal: Because bandit troubles were not yet settled, he was kept from going to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Because raids and rebellion had not yet ended, he was kept at headquarters and never took up the province.

sentences.zh: 與于謹討劉平伏，加大都督。

translations.literal: With Yu Jin he punished Liu Pingfu, and was given the added title grand area commander.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Yu Jin against Liu Pingfu and received the added title of grand area commander.

sentences.zh: 從文帝援玉壁，進儀同三司。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Wen to relieve Yubi and was advanced to opener of the way with equal third rank.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuwen Tai to the relief of Yubi and was promoted to opener of the way with equal third rank.

sentences.zh: 九年，高仲密以地來附，通從若干惠戰於邙山，衆軍皆退，唯惠與通率所部力戰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Gao Zhongmi came over with his territory; Tong followed Ruogan Hui in battle at Mount Mang; all armies withdrew—only Hui and Tong led their units in fierce fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Gao Zhongmi defected with his lands, Tong fought under Ruogan Hui at Mount Mang; every other corps fell back—only Hui and Tong held their men in hard combat.

sentences.zh: 至夜中乃陰引還，敵亦不敢逼。

translations.literal: At midnight they silently withdrew; the enemy also did not dare press them.
translations.idiomatic: Near midnight they slipped away under cover; the enemy did not dare pursue.

sentences.zh: 進授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、太僕卿，賜姓步六孤氏，進爵綏德郡公。

translations.literal: He was further invested as general of fast cavalry, opener of the way with equal third rank, and grand minister of stud; granted the surname Bulugu; rank advanced to Duke of the Commandery of Suide.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made general of fast cavalry, opener of the way with equal third rank, and grand minister of stud; granted the surname Bulugu; and raised to Duke of the Commandery of Suide.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔踐阼，拜小司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, [Tong] was appointed Junior Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne, Tong was made junior minister of works.

sentences.zh: 保定五年，累遷大司寇。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Baoding, he was promoted step by step to Grand Minister of Crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Baoding he rose through successive posts to grand minister of crime.

sentences.zh: 通性柔謹，雖久處列位，常清慎自守。

translations.literal: Tong's nature was mild and cautious; though long in high office, he always kept himself pure and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was mild and cautious by nature; though he held high rank for many years, he always maintained a scrupulous reserve.

sentences.zh: 所得祿賜，盡與親故共之，家無餘財。

translations.literal: All salary and gifts he received he shared entirely with kin and old friends; his household kept no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He gave every stipend and gift to relatives and old friends and kept no surplus at home.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「凡人患貧而不貴，不患貴而貧也。

translations.literal: He often said: "People worry about being poor rather than honored; they do not worry about being honored yet poor.
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "People fear poverty more than low rank; they do not fear high rank with empty coffers.

sentences.zh: 」建德元年，轉大司馬。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Jiande he was transferred to Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of Jiande he was moved to grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 其年薨。

translations.literal: That same year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year.

sentences.zh: 通弟逞。

translations.literal: Tong's younger brother Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's younger brother was Cheng.

sentences.zh: 逞字季明。

translations.literal: Cheng, styled Jiming.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, courtesy name Jiming.

sentences.zh: 初名彥，字世雄。

translations.literal: At first his given name was Yan and his style Shixiong.
translations.idiomatic: Originally his given name was Yan and his style Shixiong.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝常從容謂之曰：「爾旣溫裕，何因乃字世雄？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once said to him with easy grace: "You are already warm and generous—why take the style Shixiong?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once said to him at leisure, "You are already mild and generous—why style yourself Hero of the Age?

sentences.zh: 且為世之雄，非所宜也。

translations.literal: Moreover, to be a hero of the age is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: To be a hero of the age is hardly fitting.

sentences.zh: 于爾兄弟，又復不類。

translations.literal: Among your brothers as well it is out of character.
translations.idiomatic: Among your brothers it suits you even less.

sentences.zh: 」遂改焉。

translations.literal: " So it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: " The name was changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 逞少謹密，早有名譽。

translations.literal: Cheng from youth was cautious and discreet and early gained a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Cheng was careful and reserved and won an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 兄通先以軍功別受茅土，乃讓父爵中都縣伯，令逞襲之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Tong had separately received a fief for military merit, so he yielded their father's rank as Baron of Zhongdu County and had Cheng inherit it.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Tong had already received a separate fief for military merit, so he yielded their father's barony of Zhongdu and had Cheng inherit it.

sentences.zh: 起家羽林監、文帝內親信。

translations.literal: He began his career as Director of the Feathered Forest Guard and an inner trusted retainer of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as director of the Feathered Forest Guard and a trusted inner attendant of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 時輩皆以驍勇自達，唯逞獨兼文雅。

translations.literal: Men of the time all made their way through fierce courage; only Cheng combined literary refinement as well.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries all rose through martial daring; Cheng alone combined literary polish with it.

sentences.zh: 文帝由此加禮遇焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen for this reason treated him with added courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen therefore treated him with special courtesy.

sentences.zh: 大統十四年，參大丞相府軍事，尋兼記室。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Datong he joined the Grand Chancellor's staff as military adviser; soon he also served as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Datong he joined the grand chancellor's staff as military adviser and soon also served as recorder.

sentences.zh: 保定初，累遷吏部中大夫，曆

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoding, he was promoted step by step to Senior Master of the Ministry of Personnel, having served in
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Baoding he rose step by step to senior master of the Ministry of Personnel, having held

translations.literal: (Fan) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Fan]

sentences.zh: 〔蕃〕部、御伯中大夫，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，徙授司宗中大夫，轉軍司馬。

translations.literal: 〔Fan〕 Department and Senior Master of the Imperial Guard, advanced to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry and grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, transferred and appointed Senior Master of the Director of Imperial Clansmen, then moved to army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: the Fan Department and senior master of the Imperial Guard; he was promoted to grand general of the flying cavalry with a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, transferred to senior master of the Director of Imperial Clansmen, and then made army marshal.

sentences.zh: 逞幹識詳明，歷任三府，所在著績。

translations.literal: Cheng's capacity and judgment were thorough and clear; he served three great offices in succession and wherever he went left notable achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's talent and judgment were precise; he served three great offices in turn and left a record of achievement wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，進爵為公。

translations.literal: The court commended him and he was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him and he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，齊遣侍中斛斯文略、中書侍郎劉逖來聘。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, Qi sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Husiwen Lue and Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe Qi sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Husiwen Lue and Secretariat Gentleman Liu Ti on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 初修鄰好，盛選行人。

translations.literal: As neighborly relations were newly restored, envoys were chosen with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Because good relations with the neighbor were being renewed, envoys were chosen with exceptional care.

sentences.zh: 詔逞為使主，尹公正為副以報之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Cheng chief envoy and Yin Gongzheng deputy to return the visit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Cheng chief envoy and Yin Gongzheng his deputy for the return mission.

sentences.zh: 逞美容止，善辭令，敏而有禮，齊人稱焉。

translations.literal: Cheng had fine looks and bearing, was skilled in formal speech, quick yet courteous—the men of Qi praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had handsome presence, spoke well, and was quick yet courteous; the men of Qi praised him.

sentences.zh: 還屆近畿，詔令路車

translations.literal: On returning and reaching the capital vicinity, an edict ordered a court carriage
translations.idiomatic: When he returned and reached the capital outskirts, an edict ordered a court carriage with

translations.literal: (Shi) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Yi]

sentences.zh: 〔儀〕服，郊迎而入。

translations.literal: 〔Yi〕 regalia and a suburban welcome as he entered.
translations.idiomatic: ceremonial regalia and a suburban welcome for his entry.

sentences.zh: 時人榮之。

translations.literal: Men of the time regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries counted this a great honor.

sentences.zh: 四年，除京兆尹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 都界有豕生數子，經旬而死。

translations.literal: In the capital district a sow bore several piglets and died after ten-odd days.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital district a sow farrowed several piglets and died after about ten days.

sentences.zh: 其家又有豶，遂乳養之，諸豚賴之以活。

translations.literal: The household also had a boar, which then nursed them; the piglets lived by relying on him.
translations.idiomatic: The household also had a boar, which then suckled them; the piglets survived by his care.

sentences.zh: 時論以逞仁政所致。

translations.literal: Public opinion attributed this to Cheng's benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion took this as a sign of Cheng's benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 俄遷司會中大夫，出為河州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Senior Master of the Director of Accounts and sent out as Inspector of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to senior master of the Director of Accounts and sent out as inspector of He.

sentences.zh: 晉公護雅重其才，表為中外府司馬，賴委任之。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu highly valued his talent and memorialized to make him marshal of the inner-and-outer office, relying on and entrusting him.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu greatly valued his ability, memorialized to make him marshal of the inner-and-outer office, and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 尋復為司會，兼納言，遷小司馬。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Director of Accounts, concurrently Chief Censor, and promoted to Junior Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again made director of accounts, concurrently chief censor, and promoted to junior marshal.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，坐免官。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, he was stripped of office on account of association.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Hu was executed, Cheng was dismissed from office on account of the connection.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起為納言。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as Chief Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as chief censor.

sentences.zh: 又以疾不堪劇任，乃除宜州刺史。

translations.literal: Again, because illness made heavy duties unbearable, he was appointed Inspector of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Again, because illness made strenuous duties impossible, he was appointed inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 故事，刺史奉辭，例備鹵簿。

translations.literal: By precedent when an inspector took leave of the throne, a full guard-of-honor escort was standard.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent an inspector taking leave of the throne was furnished with a full guard-of-honor escort.

sentences.zh: 逞以時屬農要，奏請停之。

translations.literal: Cheng, since it was the crucial farming season, memorialized to suspend this.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, because it was the critical farming season, memorialized to dispense with it.

sentences.zh: 武帝深嘉焉，詔遂其所請，以彰雅操。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu deeply commended this; an edict granted his request to display his refined conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu greatly approved; an edict granted his request to honor his refined character.

sentences.zh: 逞在州有惠政，吏人稱之。

translations.literal: Cheng in the province had benevolent policies; officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In the province Cheng governed with kindness, and officials and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 東宮初建，授太子太保。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was first established, he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was first established, he was made grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈大將軍。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given the title Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as grand general.

sentences.zh: 子操嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 柳敏字白澤，河東解縣人，晉太常純之七世孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Min, styled Baize, was a native of Jie County in Hedong—the seventh-generation descendant of Jin's Grand Minister of Ceremonies Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Min, courtesy name Baize, came from Jie County in Hedong and was seventh in descent from Jin's Grand Minister of Ceremonies Chun.

sentences.zh: 父懿，魏車騎大將軍、儀同三司、汾州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Wei Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, equal in rank to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Inspector of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was Wei grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in rank to the Three Ducal Ministers, and inspector of Fen.

sentences.zh: 敏九歲而孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Min lost his father at nine and was known for serving his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Min was orphaned at nine and was known for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 性好學，涉獵經史，陰陽卜筮之術，靡不習焉。

translations.literal: His nature loved learning; he ranged through the classics and histories, and yin-yang divination and oracle techniques—there was none he did not study.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and ranged through the classics and histories, yin-yang lore, and divination—there was little he did not study.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，起家員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Before reaching the capped age he began his career as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Outside the Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before coming of age he entered service as regular attendant of scattered cavalry outside the office.

sentences.zh: 累遷河東郡丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Assistant Administrator of Hedong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to assistant administrator of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 朝議以敏之本邑，故有此授。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that since it was Min's home district, this appointment was made.
translations.idiomatic: The court decided that because it was his home district, he should receive the post.

sentences.zh: 敏雖統御鄉里，而處物平允，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: Though Min governed his home region, he was even-handed in dealing with affairs and won great repute at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Though he governed his own home region, he was even-handed in affairs and won wide esteem.

sentences.zh: 及文帝剋復河東，見而器異之，乃謂之曰：「今日不喜得河東，喜得卿也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen recovered Hedong, he saw Min and prized him as extraordinary, and said to him: "Today I am not glad to have Hedong—I am glad to have you.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen recovered Hedong and met Min, he marveled at him and said, "Today I am not glad to have Hedong—I am glad to have you.

sentences.zh: 」卽拜丞相府參軍事。

translations.literal: " He was at once appointed staff officer of the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately appointed staff officer of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 俄轉戶曹參軍，

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Revenue Section staff officer,
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to revenue-section staff officer,

translations.literal: (Zhang) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Jian]

sentences.zh: 〔兼〕記室。

translations.literal: 〔Jian〕 recorder.
translations.idiomatic: concurrently recorder.

sentences.zh: 每有四方賓客，恒令接之，爰及吉凶禮儀，亦令監綜。

translations.literal: Whenever there were guests from the four directions, he was always ordered to receive them; matters of auspicious and inauspicious ritual as well were placed under his supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever guests came from the four quarters he was ordered to receive them, and auspicious and mourning rites as well were placed under his oversight.

sentences.zh: 又與蘇綽等修撰新制，為朝廷政典。

translations.literal: Together with Su Chuo and others he compiled new regulations that became the court's administrative code.
translations.idiomatic: With Su Chuo and others he compiled new regulations that became the court's administrative code.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部郎中，封武城縣子，加帥都督，領本鄉兵。

translations.literal: He was moved to Bureau Director of the Ministry of Rites, enfeoffed as Viscount of Wucheng, given the added title Commander-in-Chief, and put in charge of militia from his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bureau director of the Ministry of Rites, enfeoffed Viscount of Wucheng, given the added title commander-in-chief, and put in charge of militia from his home district.

sentences.zh: 俄進大都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Grand Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to grand commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪旬日之間，鬢髮半白。

translations.literal: On his mother's death, within ten days of mourning his temples and hair turned half white.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, within ten days of mourning his temples and hair had turned half white.

sentences.zh: 尋起為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as bureau director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 毀瘠過禮，杖而後起。

translations.literal: His grief-wasting exceeded ritual propriety; only with a staff did he rise afterward.
translations.idiomatic: His mourning emaciation went beyond ritual; he could rise afterward only with a staff.

sentences.zh: 文帝見而歎異之，特加廩賜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen saw this and sighed in wonder, granting him special rations and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen saw this, sighed in admiration, and granted him special rations and gifts.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥伐蜀，以敏為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Wei Chijiong campaigned against Shu, Min was made army marshal on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Chijiong marched against Shu, Min was made campaign army marshal.

sentences.zh: 軍中籌略，並以委之。

translations.literal: All military planning in the army was entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: All military planning in the campaign was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 益州平，進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，遷尚書，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: When Yizhou was pacified, he was advanced to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, given the added title Attendant-in-Ordinary, moved to Chief Minister, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhou was pacified he was promoted to grand general of the flying cavalry with a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, made attendant-in-ordinary, moved to chief minister, and granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 六官建，拜禮部中大夫。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Senior Master of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were established he was appointed senior master of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵為公，又除河東郡守，尋復征拜禮部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced in rank to duke; he was also made Administrator of Hedong, then soon recalled and appointed again to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne he was raised to duke, made administrator of Hedong, and soon recalled again to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出為郢州刺史，甚得物情。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of E Province and won people's hearts exceedingly.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as inspector of E, he won the people's hearts completely.

sentences.zh: 及將還朝，夷夏士人感其惠政，並齎酒肴及土產候之於路。

translations.literal: When he was about to return to court, Chinese and non-Chinese gentry, moved by his benevolent rule, all brought wine, food, and local products to wait for him along the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to return to court, Chinese and non-Chinese gentry, grateful for his benevolent rule, lined the road with wine, food, and local products to see him off.

sentences.zh: 敏乃從他道而還。

translations.literal: Min then returned by another route.
translations.idiomatic: Min then went back by another route.

sentences.zh: 復拜禮部。

translations.literal: He was again appointed to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 後改禮部為司宗，仍以敏為之。

translations.literal: Later, when the Ministry of Rites was renamed Director of Imperial Clansmen, Min was still placed over it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Ministry of Rites was renamed the Director of Imperial Clansmen, Min remained in charge of it.

sentences.zh: 敏操履方正，性又恭勤，每日將朝，必夙興待旦。

translations.literal: Min's conduct was upright and his nature moreover respectful and diligent; every day before court he always rose early and waited for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Min's conduct was upright and his nature respectful and diligent; every day before court he rose early and waited for dawn.

sentences.zh: 又久處臺閣，明練故事，近

translations.literal: He had long served in the ministries and knew precedent thoroughly; recently
translations.idiomatic: Having long served in the ministries he knew precedent thoroughly; recently

translations.literal: (Yi) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Yi]

sentences.zh: 〔儀〕或乖先典者，皆按據舊章，刊正取中。

translations.literal: 〔ceremonial〕 matters that departed from ancient statutes were all checked against old rules, corrected and adjusted to the mean.
translations.idiomatic: ceremonial matters that departed from ancient statutes were all checked against old rules, corrected, and brought to a balanced standard.

sentences.zh: 遷小宗伯，監修國史。

translations.literal: He was moved to Junior Clan Commander and overseer of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was made junior clan commander and overseer of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 轉小司馬，又監修律令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Junior Marshal and again oversaw compiling statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to junior marshal and again oversaw compiling statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，出為鄜州刺史，以疾不之部。

translations.literal: He advanced to grand general, was sent out as Inspector of Fu Province, but owing to illness did not go to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to grand general, he was sent out as inspector of Fu but, owing to illness, never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 武帝平齊，進爵武德郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi, he was advanced to Duke of Wude commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi he was raised to Duke of Wude commandery.

sentences.zh: 敏自建德以後，寢疾積年，武帝及宣帝並親幸其第問疾焉。

translations.literal: From Jiande onward Min lay ill for many years; both Emperor Wu and Emperor Xuan personally visited his home to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiande onward Min was bedridden for years; both Emperor Wu and Emperor Xuan personally visited his home to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 昂字千里，幼聰穎有器識，幹局過人。

translations.literal: Ang, styled Qianli, from youth was bright and capable with foresight; his administrative talent surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, courtesy name Qianli, was clever and far-sighted from youth; his administrative talent surpassed others.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，為內史中大夫、開府儀同三司，賜爵文城郡公。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu he was Senior Master of the Internal Secretary, grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he was senior master of the Internal Secretary, held a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and was enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 當途用事，百寮皆出其下。

translations.literal: He held power at the helm; all officials ranked below him.
translations.idiomatic: He held power at court, and all officials ranked below him.

sentences.zh: 昂竭誠獻替，知無不為，謙虛自處，未嘗驕物。

translations.literal: Ang served with full loyalty and forthright counsel, doing all he knew how; he kept himself modest and never showed arrogance toward others.
translations.idiomatic: Ang served with full loyalty and frank counsel, doing all he could; he kept himself modest and never acted arrogantly toward others.

sentences.zh: 時論以此重之。

translations.literal: Men of the time for this reason held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries for this reason held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 武帝崩，受遺輔政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died, he received the dying charge and assisted in government.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died, he received the dying charge and helped govern.

sentences.zh: 稍被宣帝疏，然不離本職。

translations.literal: He was gradually kept at a distance by Emperor Xuan, yet did not leave his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan gradually kept him at a distance, yet he did not leave his original post.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，深自結納。

translations.literal: When Sui Emperor Wen was Chancellor, Ang cultivated deep ties with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Emperor Wen was chancellor, Ang cultivated close ties with him.

sentences.zh: 文帝以為大宗伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen appointed him Grand Clan Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen appointed him grand clan commander.

sentences.zh: 拜日，遂得偏風，不能視事。

translations.literal: On the day of his appointment he immediately suffered hemiplegia and could not conduct affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his appointment he suddenly suffered hemiplegia and could not perform his duties.

sentences.zh: 文帝受禪，疾愈，加上開府，拜潞州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen received the abdication, Ang recovered from illness, was given additional opening-office status, and was appointed Governor of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Ang recovered from illness, was given additional opening-office status, and was made governor of Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 昂見天下無事，上表請勸學行禮。

translations.literal: Seeing the realm at peace, Ang memorialized asking to encourage learning and practice ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm at peace, Ang memorialized asking the court to encourage learning and the practice of ritual.

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之，優詔答昂。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved; a gracious edict replied to Ang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and approved; a gracious edict answered Ang.

sentences.zh: 自是天下州縣皆置博士習禮焉。

translations.literal: From then on, prefectures and counties throughout the realm all established erudites to study ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every prefecture and county in the realm established erudites to study ritual.

sentences.zh: 昂在州甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Ang in the province had very benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Ang governed the province with marked benevolence.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away while still holding office.

sentences.zh: 子調嗣。

translations.literal: His son Diao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Diao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 盧柔字子剛。

translations.literal: Lu Rou, styled Zigang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rou, courtesy name Zigang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為叔母所養，撫視甚於其子。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was raised by his aunt, who cared for him more than for her own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was raised by his aunt, who cared for him even more than for her own sons.

sentences.zh: 柔盡心溫凊，亦同己親。

translations.literal: Rou devoted himself to warming in winter and cooling in summer, treating her as his own parent.
translations.idiomatic: Rou warmed her in winter and cooled her in summer with complete devotion, as though she were his own mother.

sentences.zh: 宗族歎重之。

translations.literal: The clan admired and esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: The clan admired and respected him.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，好學，未弱冠，解屬文，但口吃不能持論。

translations.literal: By nature clever and fond of learning, before reaching majority he could compose literary pieces, but he stuttered and could not hold forth in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and studious by nature, he could write polished prose before he came of age, but he stuttered and could not sustain an argument in speech.

sentences.zh: 頗使酒誕節，為世所譏。

translations.literal: He was rather given to wine and unrestrained conduct, and the world mocked him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He drank heavily and lived without restraint, and people mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 司徒、臨淮王彧見而器之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu saw and valued him, and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works and Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu noticed and valued him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 及魏孝武與齊神武有隙，詔賀拔勝出牧荊州，柔謂因此可著功績，遂從勝之荊州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and Gao Huan fell out, an edict sent Heba Sheng to administer Jing Province; Rou judged that he could thereby win merit and followed Sheng to Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei and Gao Huan fell out, an edict sent Heba Sheng to take charge of Jing Province; Rou thought he could win distinction by it and followed Sheng there.

sentences.zh: 以柔為大行臺郎中，掌書記。

translations.literal: Rou was made gentleman of the grand mobile headquarters in charge of records.
translations.idiomatic: Rou was made gentleman of the grand mobile headquarters and put in charge of records.

sentences.zh: 軍中機務，柔多預之。

translations.literal: In important military affairs of the army, Rou often took part.
translations.idiomatic: He often took part in the army's critical business.

sentences.zh: 及勝為太保，以柔為掾，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Sheng became grand guardian, Rou was made his staff officer with the added rank of general of the victorious army.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sheng was made grand guardian, Rou joined his staff as a general of the victorious army.

sentences.zh: 孝武后召勝引兵赴洛，勝以問柔。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xiaowu summoned Sheng to bring troops to Luoyang; Sheng asked Rou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowu summoned Sheng to bring troops to Luoyang, and Sheng asked Rou's counsel.

sentences.zh: 曰：「高歡托晉陽之甲，意實難知。

translations.literal: He said: "Gao Huan relies on the armies of Jinyang; his intent is truly hard to know.
translations.idiomatic: Rou said, "Gao Huan relies on the armies of Jinyang, and his intent is hard to read.

sentences.zh: 公宜席捲赴都，與決勝負，存沒以之，此忠之上策也。

translations.literal: My lord should sweep to the capital and decide victory or defeat with him, staking life upon it—that is the upper plan of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Your Grace should sweep to the capital, decide victory or defeat with him, and stake life on the outcome—that is the loyal upper plan.

sentences.zh: 若北阻魯陽，南幷舊楚，東連兗、豫，西接關中，帶甲十萬，觀釁而動，亦中策也。

translations.literal: If you block Luyang in the north, combine with old Chu in the south, link Yan and Yu in the east, and reach to Guanzhong in the west, with one hundred thousand armored men watch for openings and move—that too is a middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: If you hold Luyang in the north, join old Chu in the south, link Yan and Yu in the east, and tie to Guanzhong in the west, with one hundred thousand armored men watch for an opening and move—that is the middle plan.

sentences.zh: 舉三荊之地，通款梁國，可以身免，功名去矣。

translations.literal: Raise the three Jing provinces, open friendly ties with Liang—you may save yourself, but fame and achievement are gone.
translations.idiomatic: Raise the three Jing provinces and open friendly ties with Liang—you may save yourself, but fame and achievement are lost.

sentences.zh: 策之下者。

translations.literal: That is the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: That would be the least of the plans.

sentences.zh: 」勝輕柔年少，笑而不應。

translations.literal: " Sheng looked down on Rou for his youth, smiled, and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Sheng looked down on Rou for his youth, smiled, and made no answer.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，東魏遣侯景襲穰，勝敗，遂南奔梁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing to attack Xiang; Sheng was defeated and fled south to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu moved westward, Eastern Wei dispatched Hou Jing against Xiang; Sheng was routed and fled south into Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 柔亦從之。

translations.literal: Rou followed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Rou followed him.

sentences.zh: 勝頻表梁求歸，武帝覽表，嘉其辭彩。

translations.literal: Sheng repeatedly memorialized Liang asking to return north; Emperor Wu of Liang, reading the memorials, praised their literary polish.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng repeatedly memorialized Liang asking to return north; Emperor Wu of Liang read the memorials and praised their literary polish.

sentences.zh: 旣知柔所制，因遣舍人勞問，幷遺縑錦。

translations.literal: Learning they were Rou's composition, he sent a palace attendant with condolences and also bestowed silk and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Rou had written them, he sent a palace attendant with greetings and also bestowed silk and brocade.

sentences.zh: 後與勝俱還，行至襄陽，齊神武懼勝西入，遣侯景以輕騎邀之。

translations.literal: Later, returning north with Sheng, when they reached Xiangyang, Gao Huan feared Sheng would enter the west and sent Hou Jing with light cavalry to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: Later, returning north with Sheng, they reached Xiangyang; Gao Huan feared Sheng would go west and sent Hou Jing with light cavalry to cut them off.

sentences.zh: 勝及柔懼，乃棄船山行，贏糧冒險，經數百里。

translations.literal: Sheng and Rou in fear abandoned their boats and traveled by mountain paths, carrying grain on their backs through danger for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Rou, in fear, abandoned their boats and traveled by mountain paths, carrying grain on their backs through peril for several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 時屬秋霖，徒侶凍餒，死者太半。

translations.literal: It was autumn rains; followers froze and starved, and more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn rains had set in; companions froze and starved, and more than half died on the road.

sentences.zh: 至豐陽界，柔迷失道，獨宿僵木之下，寒雨衣濕，殆至於死。

translations.literal: Reaching the border of Fengyang, Rou lost the road and slept alone beneath a dead tree, cold rain soaking his clothes, nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: At the border of Fengyang, Rou lost the road and slept alone beneath a dead tree, cold rain soaking his clothes until he was near death.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，至長安。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he reached Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year two he arrived at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 封容城縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed baron of Rongcheng county with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He received enfeoffment as baron of Rongcheng county, with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太祖重其才，引為行臺郎中，加平東將軍，除從事中郎，與蘇綽對掌機密。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor valued his talent, brought him in as gentleman of the mobile headquarters, added general who pacifies the east, made him attendant gentleman, and paired him with Su Chuo to share confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai valued his talent, brought him in as gentleman of the mobile headquarters, added general who pacifies the east, made him attendant gentleman, and paired him with Su Chuo to share confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 時沙苑之後，大軍屢捷，汝、潁之間，多舉義來附。

translations.literal: At that time after Shayuan, the great army repeatedly won; between Ru and Ying, many rose in allegiance and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Shayuan the great army won again and again; between the Ru and Ying rivers many districts rose in allegiance and submitted.

sentences.zh: 書翰往反，日百餘牒。

translations.literal: Letters went back and forth—more than a hundred dispatches a day.
translations.idiomatic: Letters went back and forth at a rate of more than a hundred dispatches a day.

sentences.zh: 柔隨機報答，皆合事宜。

translations.literal: Rou answered as circumstances required, all fitting the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Rou answered as circumstances required, and every reply fit the occasion.

sentences.zh: 進爵為子，增邑三百戶，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was advanced to viscount, his fief increased by three hundred households, and he was made palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His rank rose to viscount, his fief grew by three hundred households, and he was named palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷司農少卿，轉郎，兼著作，撰起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the grand commissariat, then gentleman, concurrently compiling and writing the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of the grand commissariat, then to gentleman, and concurrently compiled the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 後拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed attendant at the yellow gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made attendant at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 文帝知其貧，解衣賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen knew he was poor and gave him his own garment off his back.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai knew he was poor and gave him the coat off his own back.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，加軍騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍、中書監。

translations.literal: In the first year of the deposed emperor of Wei, he was given the added ranks of grand general of the cavalry, equal in three departments, attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry, and supervisor of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the deposed emperor of Wei he was given the added ranks of grand general of the cavalry, equal in three departments, attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry, and supervisor of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，拜小內史，遷內史大夫，進位開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was appointed junior imperial secretary, transferred to grand imperial secretary, and advanced to opening-office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was made junior imperial secretary, then grand imperial secretary, and advanced to opening-office.

sentences.zh: 卒於位。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his post.

sentences.zh: 所作詩頌碑銘檄表啟行於世者數十篇。

translations.literal: Poems, eulogies, stele inscriptions, proclamations, memorials, and notes he wrote that circulated in the world numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of his poems, eulogies, stele inscriptions, proclamations, memorials, and notes circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 子愷嗣。

translations.literal: His son Kai succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 愷字長仁。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Changren.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, courtesy name Changren.

sentences.zh: 涉獵經史，有當世幹能。

translations.literal: He ranged through classics and histories and had practical ability for his age.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through the classics and histories and had practical ability for his age.

sentences.zh: 起家齊王記室。

translations.literal: He began his career as recorder in the household of the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His career opened as recorder in the household of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 曆吏部、內史上士，禮部下大夫。

translations.literal: He served as upper gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel and the imperial secretariat, and as lower grandee of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He held posts as upper gentleman in the Ministry of Personnel and the imperial secretariat, and as lower grandee of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋為聘陳副使。

translations.literal: Soon he was deputy envoy on a mission of courtship to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was deputy envoy on a marriage mission to Chen.

sentences.zh: 大象初，拜東京吏部下大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, he was appointed lower grandee of the Ministry of Personnel in Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Daxiang era he was made lower grandee of the Ministry of Personnel in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 唐瑾字附璘。

translations.literal: Tang Jin, styled Fulai.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jin, courtesy name Fulai.

sentences.zh: 父永。

translations.literal: His father Yong.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yong.

sentences.zh: 性溫恭，有器量，博涉經史，雅好屬文。

translations.literal: His nature was mild and respectful, with measure and capacity; he ranged broadly through classics and histories and dearly loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was mild and respectful by nature, with breadth of mind; he ranged widely through the classics and histories and dearly loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺二寸，容貌甚偉。

translations.literal: He stood eight feet two inches tall with a very imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet two inches tall and had a very imposing appearance.

sentences.zh: 年十七，周文聞其名，乃貽永書曰：「聞公有二子：曰陵，從橫多武略；

translations.literal: At age seventeen, Zhou Wen heard his name and sent Yong a letter saying: "I hear that you have two sons: Ling, versatile and rich in military stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Yuwen Tai heard of him and wrote Yong: "I hear you have two sons: Ling, versatile and full of military stratagem;

sentences.zh: 瑾，雍容富文雅。

translations.literal: Jin, dignified and rich in literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: and Jin, composed in bearing and rich in literary grace.

sentences.zh: 可並遣入朝，孤欲委以文武之任。

translations.literal: Send them both to court; I wish to entrust them with civil and military duties."
translations.idiomatic: Send them both to court; I mean to entrust them with civil and military duties."

sentences.zh: 」因召拜尚書員外郎、相府記室參軍事。

translations.literal: " He was then summoned and appointed outside-service gentleman of the masters of writing and recorder-staff officer in the chancellor's household.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he was summoned and appointed outside-service gentleman of the masters of writing and recorder-staff officer in the chancellor's household.

sentences.zh: 軍書羽檄，瑾多掌之。

translations.literal: Military letters and urgent dispatches were largely in Jin's charge.
translations.idiomatic: Military correspondence and urgent dispatches fell largely to Jin.

sentences.zh: 從破沙苑，戰河橋，並有功，封姑臧縣子。

translations.literal: Following in breaking Shayuan and fighting at He Bridge, he had merit in both and was enfeoffed viscount of Guniang county.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in breaking Shayuan and fighting at He Bridge, had merit in both, and was enfeoffed viscount of Guniang county.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書右丞、吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was progressively transferred to right assistant of the masters of writing and gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right assistant of the masters of writing and gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 于時魏室播遷，庶務草創，朝章國典，瑾並參之。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei court had been driven into exile and every affair was being built from scratch; court regulations and state statutes Jin all took part in.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Wei court had been driven into exile and every affair was being built from scratch; Jin took part in shaping court regulations and state statutes.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部尚書，進位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，賜姓宇文氏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of the grand commissariat, advanced to grand general of the agile cavalry, opening-office equal in three departments, and granted the surname Yuwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of the grand commissariat, advanced to grand general of the agile cavalry and opening-office equal in three departments, and granted the surname Yuwen.

sentences.zh: 時燕公于謹勳高望重，朝野所屬。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Yan Yu Jin had high merit and great renown, the hope of court and country.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duke of Yan Yu Jin had high merit and great renown and was the hope of court and country.

sentences.zh: 白文帝，言瑾學行兼修，願與之同姓，結為兄弟，庶子孫承其餘論，有益義方。

translations.literal: He told Emperor Wen that Jin's learning and conduct were both cultivated, that he wished to share a surname and become sworn brothers, so that posterity might inherit their mutual teaching and benefit right conduct in the family.
translations.idiomatic: He told Yuwen Tai that Jin's learning and conduct were both cultivated, that he wished to share a surname and become sworn brothers, so that their descendants might inherit their mutual teaching and benefit right conduct in the family.

sentences.zh: 文帝歎異者久之，更賜瑾姓

translations.literal: Emperor Wen marveled for a long while, then further granted Jin the surname
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marveled for a long while, then further granted Jin the surname

translations.literal: (Wan) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Wan]

sentences.zh: 〔万〕紐于氏。

translations.literal: [Wan] of the Niuyu clan.
translations.idiomatic: of the Niuyu clan.

sentences.zh: 瑾乃深相結納，敦長幼之序；

translations.literal: Jin then bonded with him deeply and honored the order of elder and younger;
translations.idiomatic: Jin then formed a deep bond with him and upheld the proper order between elder and younger;

sentences.zh: 謹亦庭羅子孫，行弟侄之敬。

translations.literal: Yu also gathered his descendants in the courtyard and observed the respect due between younger brothers and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: Yu in turn gathered his descendants in the courtyard to observe the respect due between younger brothers and nephews.

sentences.zh: 其為朝望所宗如此。

translations.literal: Thus he was revered by the hopes of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he was revered by the leading men of the court.

sentences.zh: 進爵臨淄縣伯，轉吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was advanced to baron of Linzi county and transferred to minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His peerage rose to baron of Linzi county and he was transferred to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 銓綜衡流，雅有人倫之鑒。

translations.literal: In weighing and judging the current of men, he had fine discernment in human relations.
translations.idiomatic: In weighing and judging men, he had fine discernment in human relations.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去職，尋起令視事。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left office; soon recalled and ordered to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he left office; soon he was recalled and ordered to resume duties.

sentences.zh: 時六尚書皆一時之秀，周文自謂得人，號為六俊。

translations.literal: At the time all six ministers were talents of the age; Zhou Wen considered that he had found his men and called them the Six Outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all six ministers were talents of the age; Yuwen Tai considered that he had found his men and called them the Six Outstanding.

sentences.zh: 然瑾尤見器重。

translations.literal: Yet Jin was especially trusted and valued.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin above all won his trust and regard.

sentences.zh: 于謹南伐江陵，以瑾為元帥府長史。

translations.literal: When Yu Jin marched south against Jiangling, Jin was made chief clerk of the commander-in-chief's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin marched south against Jiangling, Jin was appointed chief clerk of the commander-in-chief's office.

sentences.zh: 軍中謀略，多出瑾焉。

translations.literal: Army stratagems largely came from Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the army's stratagems originated with Jin.

sentences.zh: 江陵旣平，衣冠仕伍，並沒為僕隸。

translations.literal: Once Jiangling was pacified, gentry and common soldiers alike were seized as bond-servants.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, gentry and rank-and-file alike were seized as bond-servants.

sentences.zh: 瑾察其才行，有片善者，輒議免之，賴瑾獲濟者甚衆。

translations.literal: Jin examined their conduct and ability; where any trace of good appeared, he would propose release—many owed their deliverance to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin examined their conduct and ability; where any trace of merit appeared, he would propose release, and many owed their deliverance to him.

sentences.zh: 時論多焉。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion praised this greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised this at length.

sentences.zh: 及軍還，諸將多因虜掠，大獲財物。

translations.literal: When the army returned, many generals through plunder of captives had gained great stores of goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, many generals had gained great stores of goods through plunder of captives.

sentences.zh: 瑾一無所取，唯得書兩車，載之以歸。

translations.literal: Jin took nothing, obtaining only two cartloads of books, which he carried home.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took nothing for himself, obtaining only two cartloads of books, which he carried home.

sentences.zh: 或白文帝曰：「唐瑾大有輜重，悉是梁朝珍玩。

translations.literal: Someone reported to Emperor Wen: "Tang Jin has great baggage trains, all Liang court treasures and curios.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported to Yuwen Tai, "Tang Jin has great baggage trains, all Liang court treasures and curios.

sentences.zh: 」文帝初不信之，然欲明其虛實，密遣使檢閱之，唯見墳籍而已。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen at first did not believe it, but wishing to clarify fact from falsehood, secretly sent an envoy to inspect; only books were seen.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuwen Tai at first did not believe it, but wishing to clarify fact from falsehood, secretly sent an envoy to inspect; only books were found.

sentences.zh: 乃歎曰：「孤知此人來二十許年，明其不以利干義。

translations.literal: He then sighed and said: "I have known this man for some twenty years and understand that he does not let profit bend principle.
translations.idiomatic: He then sighed and said, "I have known this man for some twenty years and understand that he does not let profit bend principle.

sentences.zh: 向若不令檢視，恐常人有投杼之疑，所以益明之耳。

translations.literal: Had I not ordered inspection, I feared ordinary people would have the suspicion of casting away the shuttle—therefore I made it clearer still.
translations.idiomatic: Had I not ordered an inspection, I feared ordinary people would harbor the suspicion of the mother who cast away her shuttle—therefore I made the truth clearer still.

sentences.zh: 凡受人委任，當如此也。

translations.literal: All who accept another's trust ought to be like this.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who accepts another's trust ought to conduct himself in this way.

sentences.zh: 」論平江陵功，進爵為公。

translations.literal: " For merit in pacifying Jiangling, he was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: " For merit in pacifying Jiangling, he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 六官建，授禮部中大夫，出為蔡州刺史。

translations.literal: When the six offices were established, he was appointed lower grandee of the Ministry of Rites and sent out as governor of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With the establishment of the six offices, he was made lower grandee of the Ministry of Rites and sent out to govern Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷

translations.literal: He served in
translations.idiomatic: He also served as governor of

translations.literal: (Zhe) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Zhe]

sentences.zh: 〔拓〕州、硤州，所在皆有德化，人吏稱之。
