translations.literal: [Tuo] Prefecture and Xia Prefecture; everywhere he exercised virtuous influence, and officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo Prefecture and Xia Prefecture; everywhere he governed with virtuous influence, and officials and the people praised him.

sentences.zh: 轉荊州總管府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of the general headquarters of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as chief clerk of the general headquarters of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部中大夫，歷御正、納言中大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as lower grandee of the Ministry of Personnel, then served as lower grandee of the Imperial Rectifier and the Censor of Speech.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as lower grandee of the Ministry of Personnel and went on to serve as lower grandee of the Imperial Rectifier and the Censor of Speech.

sentences.zh: 曾未十旬，遂遷四職，搢紳以為榮。

translations.literal: Within not yet ten weeks he passed through four posts; gentry and officials took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: In fewer than ten weeks he passed through four posts; gentry and officials counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 久之，除司宗中大夫，兼內史。

translations.literal: After some time, he was appointed master-of-clans middle grandee, concurrently Inner Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Tang Jin was made master-of-clans middle grandee and concurrently Inner Scribe.

sentences.zh: 尋卒于位。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died while holding his post.

sentences.zh: 贈小宗伯，諡曰方。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted lesser director of the clan; posthumous name Fang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made lesser director of the clan, with the posthumous name Fang.

sentences.zh: 瑾性方重，有風格。

translations.literal: Jin by nature was square and weighty; he had style.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jin was upright and dignified by nature and had real bearing.

sentences.zh: 退朝休

translations.literal: After returning from court, rest
translations.idiomatic: When he left court on his

translations.literal: (Leisure) [emended: Leave]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: xiá]

sentences.zh: 〔假〕，恒著衣冠以對妻子。

translations.literal: 〔Leave〕, he always wore cap and robes when facing wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: days off he always wore cap and robes when with wife and children.

sentences.zh: 遇迅雷風烈，雖閑夜宴寢，必起，冠帶端笏危坐。

translations.literal: When thunder pealed and violent wind blew, even on quiet nights at leisure in bed, he would rise, put on cap and sash, hold the tablet upright, and sit formally.
translations.idiomatic: When thunder crashed and winds howled, even in the dead of night at rest in bed he would rise, put on cap and sash, hold his tablet upright, and sit formally.

sentences.zh: 又好施與，家無餘財，所得祿賜，常散之宗族。

translations.literal: He also loved giving; the household had no surplus wealth; salary and gifts received he regularly distributed among the clan.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved to give. The household kept no surplus wealth, and whatever salary and gifts he received he regularly shared among his clan.

sentences.zh: 其尤貧者，又割膏腴田宇以賑之。

translations.literal: For those most impoverished, he further cut off fertile fields and houses to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: For the poorest among them he even carved off fertile fields and houses to relieve their want.

sentences.zh: 所留遺子孫者，並磽埆之地。

translations.literal: What he left to descendants was all barren, stony land.
translations.idiomatic: What he left his descendants was nothing but poor, stony soil.

sentences.zh: 朝野以此稱之。

translations.literal: Court and countryside praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside alike praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 撰《新儀》十篇。

translations.literal: He composed New Rites in ten chapters.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote New Rites in ten chapters.

sentences.zh: 所著賦頌碑誄二十餘萬言。

translations.literal: Writings including fu, eulogies, stele inscriptions, and dirges totaled more than two hundred thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: His fu, eulogies, stele inscriptions, and dirges together ran to more than two hundred thousand words.

sentences.zh: 孫大智嗣。

translations.literal: His grandson Dazhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Dazhi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 瑾次子令則，性好篇章，兼解音律，文多輕豔，為時人所傳。

translations.literal: Jin's second son Lingze by nature loved literary composition; he also understood musical pitch; his writings were largely light and ornate and were passed around by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jin's second son Lingze loved literary composition by nature, also understood musical pitch, and wrote in a florid, showy style that men of the day passed around.

sentences.zh: 天和中，以齊馭下大夫使於陳。

translations.literal: In Tianhe, holding the rank of Qi charioteer lower grandee, he served as envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianhe era he went as envoy to Chen while holding the rank of Qi charioteer lower grandee.

sentences.zh: 大象中，官至樂部下大夫。

translations.literal: In Daxiang, he reached the post of Music Bureau lower grandee.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he rose to Music Bureau lower grandee.

sentences.zh: 仕隋，位太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Serving Sui, he held the post of Left Assistant to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui he served as Left Assistant to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇廢，被誅。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed, Tang Lingze was executed.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
